question: According to the manual, how are traffic emergencies and vehicle emergencies different?
choice_a: There is no real difference between the two
choice_b: Vehicle emergencies are always the driver's fault, while traffic emergencies never are
choice_c: Traffic emergencies occur when two vehicles are about to collide; vehicle emergencies occur when tires, brakes, or other critical parts fail
choice_d: Traffic emergencies only happen at night; vehicle emergencies only happen during the day
explanation: The manual states traffic emergencies occur when two vehicles are about to collide, while vehicle emergencies occur when tires, brakes, or other critical parts fail.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Driving Emergencies

question: Why does the manual say stopping is not always the safest action in an emergency?
choice_a: Because brakes should never be used on a commercial vehicle
choice_b: Because you can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop
choice_c: Because state law requires steering around all obstacles
choice_d: Because stopping always causes a jackknife
explanation: The manual explains that when you don't have enough room to stop, you may have to steer away, since you can almost always turn to miss an obstacle more quickly than you can stop.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: Why does the manual say you should keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times?
choice_a: It prevents the ABS malfunction lamp from coming on
choice_b: So you have a firm grip to turn quickly if an emergency requires it
choice_c: It keeps the parking brake from engaging accidentally
choice_d: It is required only when driving over 55 mph
explanation: The manual states that to turn quickly in an emergency you must have a firm grip on the wheel with both hands, so the best practice is to keep both hands on the wheel at all times.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: What does the manual warn can happen if you apply the brake while turning sharply in an emergency?
choice_a: The ABS will disengage completely
choice_b: The steering wheel will automatically counter-steer
choice_c: It's very easy to lock your wheels and skid out of control
choice_d: Nothing; braking while turning is always safe
explanation: The manual warns not to apply the brake while turning because it is very easy to lock your wheels, which can cause you to skid out of control.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: Why does the manual say not to turn the steering wheel more than needed to clear an obstacle?
choice_a: It will trigger the trailer's ABS malfunction lamp
choice_b: It has no effect on skid or rollover risk
choice_c: The more sharply you turn, the greater the chances of a skid or rollover
choice_d: Sharp turns cause the fuel tank to overheat
explanation: The manual states you should not turn any more than needed to clear the obstacle, because the more sharply you turn, the greater the chances of a skid or rollover.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: What is 'counter-steering' as described in the manual?
choice_a: Steering with one hand to save time
choice_b: A technique used only on vehicles without ABS
choice_c: Applying the parking brake while turning
choice_d: Turning the wheel back in the other direction once you've passed whatever was in your path
explanation: The manual describes counter-steering as turning the wheel back the other way once you've passed the obstacle, and treats emergency steering and counter-steering as two parts of one driving action.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: If an oncoming driver has drifted into your lane, which way does the manual say you should steer?
choice_a: It does not matter which way you steer
choice_b: You should always brake instead of steering
choice_c: To your left, into the oncoming lane
choice_d: To your right
explanation: The manual recommends moving to your right if an oncoming driver has drifted into your lane, since that driver's natural response will likely be to return to their own lane.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: If forced to leave the road onto the shoulder, what does the manual say about braking?
choice_a: Apply the brakes as hard as possible immediately
choice_b: Never brake at all until you are back on the pavement
choice_c: Avoid using the brakes until your speed has dropped to about 20 mph, then brake gently
choice_d: Use only the parking brake on a shoulder
explanation: The manual advises avoiding braking on the shoulder until speed drops to about 20 mph, then braking very gently to avoid skidding on a loose surface.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: When returning to the road from the shoulder, what does the manual say you should NOT do?
choice_a: Hold the wheel tightly and turn sharply enough to get back onto the road safely
choice_b: Check your mirrors and signal before pulling back onto the road
choice_c: Try to edge gradually back onto the road, because your tires might grab unexpectedly and cause loss of control
choice_d: Counter-steer once both front tires are back on the paved surface
explanation: The manual warns against edging gradually back onto the road because your tires might grab unexpectedly and you could lose control; instead, turn sharply enough to get back on safely.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Steering to Avoid a Crash

question: What is the 'controlled braking' method described in the manual?
choice_a: Applying the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels, keeping steering movements small
choice_b: Using only the parking brake to slow down
choice_c: Applying the brakes fully and releasing only when wheels lock, then reapplying fully
choice_d: Pumping the brakes rapidly in short bursts
explanation: With controlled braking, the manual says you apply the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels, keeping steering wheel movements very small.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, How to Stop Quickly and Safely

question: What is the 'stab braking' method described in the manual?
choice_a: Applying the brakes fully, releasing when the wheels lock up, then reapplying fully once the wheels start rolling again
choice_b: Applying the parking brake and hydraulic brake at the same time
choice_c: Tapping the brakes lightly at regular intervals regardless of wheel lock
choice_d: Braking only with the trailer brakes
explanation: The manual describes stab braking as applying the brakes all the way, releasing when the wheels lock up, and reapplying fully as soon as the wheels start rolling.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, How to Stop Quickly and Safely

question: What does the manual say about jamming on the brakes in an emergency?
choice_a: Jamming on the brakes is only dangerous on wet roads
choice_b: Jamming on the brakes is the recommended emergency braking technique
choice_c: Pushing down on the brake pedal as hard as you can will only keep the wheels locked up and cause a skid
choice_d: Jamming on the brakes always shortens stopping distance safely
explanation: The manual explains that emergency braking does not mean pushing the pedal as hard as possible, because that will keep the wheels locked and cause a skid, and skidding wheels cannot be controlled.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, How to Stop Quickly and Safely

question: According to the manual, what are the two most common causes of hydraulic brake failure?
choice_a: ABS malfunction and a broken speedometer
choice_b: Overinflated tires and a dead battery
choice_c: Loss of hydraulic pressure and brake fade on long hills
choice_d: Worn tires and low fuel
explanation: The manual states most hydraulic brake failures occur due to loss of hydraulic pressure or brake fade on long hills.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Brake Failure

question: When using the parking/emergency brake to slow a vehicle with hydraulic brake failure, what must you also do?
choice_a: Disconnect the trailer
choice_b: Shift into neutral first
choice_c: Turn off the engine before applying it
choice_d: Press the release button or pull the release lever at the same time so you can adjust brake pressure and keep the wheels from locking
explanation: The manual instructs that when using the parking/emergency brake, you must press the release button or pull the release lever at the same time so you can adjust brake pressure and keep the wheels from locking up.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Brake Failure

question: After stopping a vehicle by turning uphill following brake failure, what precaution does the manual mention?
choice_a: Immediately restart the engine and continue driving
choice_b: Disconnect the trailer brakes
choice_c: Make sure the vehicle does not start rolling backward, put it in low gear, apply the parking brake, and roll back into an obstacle if necessary
choice_d: Leave the vehicle in neutral with no brakes applied
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to make sure the vehicle does not roll backward after stopping uphill, put it in low gear, apply the parking brake, and if necessary roll back into an obstacle that will stop the vehicle.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Brake Failure

question: What is an escape ramp, according to the manual?
choice_a: A ramp, usually located a few miles from the top of a downgrade, that uses soft gravel or an uphill grade to bring a runaway vehicle to a stop
choice_b: A designated area for changing flat tires
choice_c: A paved lane reserved for buses only
choice_d: A ramp used exclusively by emergency vehicles responding to a crash
explanation: The manual describes escape ramps as usually located a few miles from the top of a downgrade, using soft gravel that resists motion or an uphill grade with gravel to stop and hold the vehicle.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Brake Failure

question: What is the loud 'bang' sound a major sign of, according to the manual's discussion of tire failure?
choice_a: A blowout
choice_b: An engine backfire that never indicates a tire problem
choice_c: A fuel line leak
choice_d: An ABS malfunction
explanation: The manual identifies the loud 'bang' of a blowout as an easily recognized sign of tire failure, and says any time you hear a tire blow, assume it is yours.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Tire Failure

question: When a front tire fails, what does the manual say you must do to prevent the steering wheel from being twisted out of your hand?
choice_a: Shift into neutral
choice_b: Apply the brakes immediately and hold them
choice_c: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands at all times
choice_d: Release the wheel and let it correct itself
explanation: The manual states the only way to prevent a front tire failure from twisting the wheel out of your hands is to keep a firm grip with both hands at all times.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Tire Failure

question: What does the manual say about braking immediately after a tire fails?
choice_a: Brake as hard as possible immediately to stop before losing more control
choice_b: Stay off the brake, unless about to run into something, until the vehicle has slowed, then brake gently
choice_c: Only use the parking brake after a tire failure
choice_d: Braking has no effect on a vehicle with a failed tire
explanation: The manual explains that braking when a tire has failed could cause loss of control, so you should stay off the brake until the vehicle has slowed, unless you're about to hit something.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Tire Failure

question: What does the manual say ABS does?
choice_a: It replaces the need for regular brake maintenance
choice_b: It is a computerized system that keeps your wheels from locking up during hard brake applications
choice_c: It increases your normal braking capability
choice_d: It automatically steers the vehicle around obstacles
explanation: The manual defines ABS as a computerized system that keeps your wheels from locking up during hard brake applications.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: Does ABS necessarily shorten your stopping distance, according to the manual?
choice_a: No, but it does help you keep the vehicle under control during hard braking
choice_b: ABS only affects stopping distance on dry pavement
choice_c: Yes, ABS always shortens stopping distance
choice_d: ABS has no effect on control or stopping distance
explanation: The manual explicitly states ABS does not necessarily shorten your stopping distance, but it does help you keep the vehicle under control during hard braking.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Antilock Braking Systems (ABS)

question: How does the ABS electronic control unit (ECU) respond when sensors detect potential wheel lock-up?
choice_a: It increases brake pressure to force the wheels to stop turning
choice_b: It decreases brake pressure to avoid wheel lock-up
choice_c: It disengages the parking brake
choice_d: It shuts off the engine
explanation: The manual explains that sensors detect potential wheel lock-up and the ECU decreases brake pressure to avoid it, adjusting pressure to provide maximum braking without lockup.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, How Antilock Braking Systems Work

question: Which truck tractors does the Department of Transportation require to have ABS?
choice_a: Truck tractors with hydraulic brakes built after 2000
choice_b: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997
choice_c: All truck tractors regardless of build date
choice_d: Only truck tractors built before 1990
explanation: The manual states the DOT requires ABS on truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Vehicles Required to Have Antilock Braking Systems

question: Where are the yellow ABS malfunction lamps located on trailers, according to the manual?
choice_a: Inside the cab on the instrument panel
choice_b: On the left side, either on the front or rear corner
choice_c: On the underside of the trailer only, not visible from outside
choice_d: On the right side only
explanation: The manual states trailers will have yellow ABS malfunction lamps on the left side, either on the front or rear corner.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, How to Know If Your Vehicle Is Equipped with ABS

question: What does it mean if the ABS malfunction lamp stays on after the start-up bulb check, or comes on once you're underway?
choice_a: The vehicle's headlights need replacing
choice_b: The parking brake is engaged
choice_c: The fuel tank is nearly empty
choice_d: You may have lost ABS control
explanation: The manual states that if the lamp stays on after the bulb check or goes on once underway, you may have lost ABS control.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, How to Know If Your Vehicle Is Equipped with ABS

question: When you brake hard on a slippery surface in a vehicle WITHOUT ABS and your steering wheels lock up, what happens according to the manual?
choice_a: The brakes disengage completely
choice_b: The vehicle automatically corrects its path
choice_c: You lose steering control
choice_d: Nothing changes; steering control is unaffected
explanation: The manual explains that when steering wheels lock up during hard braking, you lose steering control, which is one of the problems ABS is designed to help prevent.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, How ABS Helps You

question: What does the manual say ABS should help you do, even if it does not always stop you faster?
choice_a: Eliminate the need for tire tread
choice_b: Accelerate more quickly out of a skid
choice_c: Steer around an obstacle while braking, and avoid skids caused by over braking
choice_d: Drive safely without checking mirrors
explanation: The manual states you may or may not stop faster with ABS, but you should be able to steer around an obstacle while braking and avoid over-braking skids.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, How ABS Helps You

question: According to the manual, what should you do when only the tractor has ABS and the trailer begins to swing out?
choice_a: There is nothing you can do if only the tractor has ABS
choice_b: Keep your eye on the trailer and let up on the brakes, if you can safely do so
choice_c: Accelerate to straighten the trailer
choice_d: Apply the trailer hand valve fully
explanation: The manual advises that when only the tractor has ABS, you should watch the trailer and let up on the brakes, if it's safe, if the trailer begins to swing out.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, ABS on the Tractor Only or Only on the Trailer

question: What does the manual say about a vehicle with ABS on only the trailer?
choice_a: It eliminates all risk of jackknifing
choice_b: It provides no benefit at all over having no ABS
choice_c: It allows you to brake harder than with full ABS
choice_d: The trailer is less likely to swing out, but if you lose steering control or start a tractor jackknife, let up on the brakes if safe
explanation: The manual states that when only the trailer has ABS, the trailer is less likely to swing out, but the driver should let up on the brakes if steering control is lost or a tractor jackknife starts.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, ABS on the Tractor Only or Only on the Trailer

question: How should you brake in a vehicle equipped with ABS, according to the manual?
choice_a: Always stab the brakes repeatedly
choice_b: Pump the brakes continuously even under normal conditions
choice_c: The same way you always have, using only the braking force necessary to stop safely and stay in control
choice_d: Always apply maximum brake pressure immediately regardless of conditions
explanation: The manual states that when driving a vehicle with ABS, you should brake as you always have, using only the braking force necessary to stop safely and stay in control.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Braking with ABS

question: What is the one exception the manual gives allowing full brake application in an emergency stop?
choice_a: Any vehicle traveling under 30 mph
choice_b: Any vehicle with a hazardous materials placard
choice_c: A straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles
choice_d: Vehicles without ABS at all
explanation: The manual states that if you drive a straight truck or combination with working ABS on all axles, you can fully apply the brakes in an emergency stop.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Braking with ABS

question: According to the manual's safety reminders, will ABS allow you to drive faster, follow more closely, or drive less carefully?
choice_a: Only in wet weather
choice_b: Yes, ABS is designed specifically to allow closer following distances
choice_c: No, ABS won't allow any of those things
choice_d: Only at highway speeds
explanation: The manual explicitly warns that ABS won't allow you to drive faster, follow more closely, or drive less carefully.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Safety Reminders

question: According to the manual, a skid happens whenever the tires lose their grip on the road. Which of the following is NOT listed as one of the four causes?
choice_a: Over-braking
choice_b: Over-steering
choice_c: Over-acceleration
choice_d: Low tire pressure alone, unrelated to speed or braking
explanation: The manual lists the four causes of skids as over-braking, over-steering, over-acceleration, and driving too fast; low tire pressure alone is not listed as one of the four causes.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Skid Control and Recovery

question: What does the manual identify as the cause of most serious skids?
choice_a: Using cruise control on the highway
choice_b: Driving too fast for road conditions
choice_c: Driving with a lightly loaded trailer
choice_d: Overinflated tires
explanation: The manual states that most serious skids result from driving too fast for road conditions, and drivers who adjust to conditions avoid over-accelerating, over-braking, or over-steering.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Skid Control and Recovery

question: What is the most common type of skid, according to the manual?
choice_a: One in which the front wheels lose traction due to worn steering components
choice_b: One caused only by high winds
choice_c: One caused by overinflated front tires
choice_d: One in which the rear wheels lose traction through excessive braking or acceleration
explanation: The manual states that by far the most common skid is one in which the rear wheels lose traction through excessive braking or acceleration.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Drive-wheel Skids

question: According to the manual, how can you easily stop an acceleration skid?
choice_a: Turn the steering wheel sharply
choice_b: Apply the brakes as hard as possible
choice_c: Shift into a higher gear immediately
choice_d: Take your foot off the accelerator
explanation: The manual states that taking your foot off the accelerator can easily stop acceleration-caused skids.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Drive-wheel Skids

question: What happens in a rear-wheel braking skid, according to the manual?
choice_a: The vehicle automatically corrects itself without driver input
choice_b: The trailer brakes engage independently of the tractor
choice_c: The front wheels lock up and slide sideways
choice_d: Locked rear wheels have less traction than rolling wheels and slide sideways trying to 'catch up' with the front wheels
explanation: The manual explains that rear wheel braking skids occur when locked rear wheels, having less traction than rolling wheels, slide sideways in an attempt to catch up with the front wheels.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Drive-wheel Skids

question: In a vehicle towing a trailer, what can a drive-wheel skid cause, according to the manual?
choice_a: Nothing different than in a straight truck
choice_b: The trailer will always detach from the tractor
choice_c: The trailer can push the towing vehicle sideways, causing a sudden jackknife
choice_d: The trailer brakes will automatically release
explanation: The manual explains that with vehicles towing trailers, a drive-wheel skid can let the trailer push the towing vehicle sideways, causing a sudden jackknife.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Drive-wheel Skids

question: What is the first step the manual gives for correcting a drive-wheel braking skid?
choice_a: Turn off the ABS system manually
choice_b: Accelerate to regain traction
choice_c: Stop braking, which lets the rear wheels roll again and keeps them from sliding
choice_d: Apply the brakes harder to force the wheels to grip
explanation: The manual states the first step to correct a drive-wheel braking skid is to stop braking, which lets the rear wheels roll again and keeps them from sliding.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Correcting a Drive-wheel Braking Skid

question: In a front-wheel skid, what happens regardless of how much you turn the steering wheel, according to the manual?
choice_a: The trailer detaches from the tractor
choice_b: The vehicle will always spin a full 360 degrees
choice_c: The rear wheels lock up automatically
choice_d: The front end tends to go in a straight line
explanation: The manual explains that in a front-wheel skid, the front end tends to go in a straight line regardless of how much you turn the steering wheel.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Front-wheel Skids

question: What is the only way to stop a front-wheel skid, according to the manual?
choice_a: Turn the steering wheel more sharply in the direction of the skid
choice_b: Stop turning and/or braking so hard, and let the vehicle slow down
choice_c: Apply full brake pressure immediately
choice_d: Accelerate out of the skid
explanation: The manual states that when a front-wheel skid occurs, the only way to stop it is to let the vehicle slow down by stopping turning and/or braking so hard.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Front-wheel Skids

question: What are the three basic steps the manual lists for any accident when you are not seriously hurt?
choice_a: Move all vehicles immediately, leave the scene, file a report later
choice_b: Call your dispatcher, take photos, exchange insurance information
choice_c: Assess damage, argue fault, wait for a tow truck
choice_d: Protect the area, notify authorities, care for the injured
explanation: The manual lists the basic accident steps as protecting the area, notifying authorities, and caring for the injured.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Accident Procedures

question: What is the first thing to do at an accident scene, according to the manual?
choice_a: Take detailed photographs of the damage
choice_b: Keep another accident from happening in the same spot
choice_c: Exchange contact information with other drivers
choice_d: Call your company's insurance provider
explanation: The manual states that the first thing to do at an accident scene is to keep another accident from happening in the same spot.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Protect the Area

question: If your vehicle is involved in the accident, what does the manual advise doing to help protect the area?
choice_a: Push it into the opposing lane to warn oncoming traffic
choice_b: Try to get it to the side of the road to prevent another accident and allow traffic to move
choice_c: Remove it from the scene entirely before police arrive
choice_d: Leave it exactly where it stopped, blocking traffic until police arrive
explanation: The manual advises trying to get your vehicle to the side of the road, which helps prevent another accident and allows traffic to move.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Protect the Area

question: What two things does the manual say to use to warn other traffic and protect the accident area?
choice_a: A cell phone flashlight and hand signals
choice_b: Brake lights only
choice_c: Flashers and reflective triangles
choice_d: Headlights and the horn only
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to put on flashers and set out reflective triangles to warn other traffic, positioned so other drivers can see them in time to avoid the accident.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Protect the Area

question: If you have a cell phone or CB at an accident scene, when does the manual say you should call for assistance?
choice_a: Calling for help is optional if the accident looks minor
choice_b: Only after caring for all injured persons
choice_c: Before you get out of your vehicle
choice_d: Only after moving all vehicles from the scene
explanation: The manual states that if you have a cell phone or CB, you should call for assistance before you get out of your vehicle.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Notify Authorities

question: If a qualified person is already helping the injured at an accident scene, what does the manual advise?
choice_a: Leave the scene immediately
choice_b: Stay out of the way unless asked to assist
choice_c: Take over the care of the injured regardless of qualifications
choice_d: Call additional emergency services even if already notified
explanation: The manual advises that if a qualified person is helping the injured, you should stay out of the way unless asked to assist.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Care for the Injured

question: When should you move a severely injured person, according to the manual?
choice_a: Always, to make them more comfortable
choice_b: Never, under any circumstances
choice_c: Only if a police officer is present
choice_d: Only if the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary
explanation: The manual states you should not move a severely injured person unless the danger of fire or passing traffic makes it necessary.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Care for the Injured

question: Which of the following does the manual list as a cause of vehicle fires related to fuel?
choice_a: A fully charged fire extinguisher
choice_b: Driver smoking, improper fueling, or loose fuel connections
choice_c: Overinflated tires
choice_d: Proper cargo ventilation
explanation: The manual lists driver smoking, improper fueling, and loose fuel connections as fuel-related causes of vehicle fires.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Causes of Fire

question: During a vehicle inspection for fire prevention, what should you be sure to check regarding the fire extinguisher?
choice_a: That it is stored in the trailer, not the cab
choice_b: That it is empty and lightweight
choice_c: That it has been used at least once
choice_d: That it is charged
explanation: The manual states that during a complete vehicle inspection, you should be sure to check that the fire extinguisher is charged.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fire Prevention

question: Where does the manual say you should park if you need to stop because of a vehicle fire?
choice_a: Under an overpass for shelter
choice_b: In a parking garage
choice_c: In an open area, away from buildings, trees, brush, other vehicles, or anything else that might catch fire
choice_d: As close as possible to the nearest service station
explanation: The manual instructs parking in an open area away from buildings, trees, brush, other vehicles, or anything that might catch fire.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fire Fighting

question: What does the manual explicitly say NOT to do if you have a vehicle fire?
choice_a: Notify emergency services
choice_b: Pull into a service station
choice_c: Turn off the engine for an engine fire
choice_d: Keep the cargo doors shut on a van fire
explanation: The manual explicitly instructs, 'Don't pull into a service station!' when dealing with a vehicle fire.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fire Fighting

question: For an engine fire, what does the manual say to avoid doing if possible?
choice_a: Shooting foam through the louvers
choice_b: Opening the hood
choice_c: Turning off the engine
choice_d: Notifying emergency services
explanation: The manual instructs that for an engine fire, you should turn off the engine as soon as you can, but should not open the hood if you can avoid it.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fire Fighting

question: How does the manual recommend fighting an engine fire without opening the hood?
choice_a: Pour water directly onto the engine block
choice_b: Disconnect the battery and leave the vehicle immediately
choice_c: Wait for the fire to burn itself out with the hood closed
choice_d: Shoot foam through the louvers, radiator, or from the vehicle's underside
explanation: The manual recommends shooting foam through the louvers, radiator, or from the vehicle's underside to fight an engine fire without opening the hood.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fire Fighting

question: Why does the manual say to keep the doors shut on a cargo fire in a van or box trailer, especially with hazardous materials?
choice_a: It has no effect on how the fire burns
choice_b: Opening the doors will supply the fire with oxygen and can cause it to burn very fast
choice_c: Keeping the doors shut prevents the fire from ever needing extinguishing
choice_d: It is required so bystanders cannot see the fire
explanation: The manual explains that opening the van doors supplies the fire with oxygen, which can cause it to burn very fast, especially with hazardous cargo.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fire Fighting

question: What is a B:C type fire extinguisher designed to work on, according to the manual?
choice_a: Wood, paper, and cloth only
choice_b: Electrical fires and burning liquids
choice_c: Only ordinary combustibles like paper
choice_d: Combustible metal fires only
explanation: The manual states the B:C type fire extinguisher is designed to work on electrical fires and burning liquids.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fire Fighting

question: Why does the manual say not to use water on a gasoline fire?
choice_a: It will spread the flames
choice_b: Gasoline fires cannot be extinguished by any method
choice_c: Water will immediately extinguish it, so it is unnecessary to use an extinguisher
choice_d: Water reacts explosively with all liquid fuels
explanation: The manual warns that water should not be used on a gasoline fire because it will spread the flames.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fire Fighting

question: If you're not sure what extinguishing agent to use, especially on a hazardous materials fire, what does the manual advise?
choice_a: Use water regardless of the type of fire
choice_b: Try to smother the fire with cargo tarps
choice_c: Wait for firefighters
choice_d: Use any extinguisher available immediately
explanation: The manual advises that if you're not sure what to use, especially on a hazardous materials fire, you should wait for firefighters.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fire Fighting

question: Does the absence of smoke or flame mean a fire cannot restart, according to the manual?
choice_a: The manual does not address this
choice_b: Yes, absence of smoke always means the fire is permanently out
choice_c: No, you should continue efforts until whatever was burning has been cooled
choice_d: Only combustible metal fires can restart after appearing out
explanation: The manual warns that the absence of smoke or flame does not mean the fire cannot restart, so you should continue until whatever was burning has been cooled.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Fire Fighting

question: According to the manual, roughly how many deaths per year result from traffic accidents involving people who drink alcohol?
choice_a: Exactly 1,000
choice_b: About 500
choice_c: Over 20,000
choice_d: Fewer than 100
explanation: The manual states that people who drink alcohol are involved in traffic accidents resulting in over 20,000 deaths every year.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol and Driving

question: How much alcohol can the human liver process per hour, according to the manual?
choice_a: There is no limit; the liver processes alcohol instantly
choice_b: About one-third of an ounce
choice_c: Exactly one full standard drink
choice_d: About three full ounces
explanation: The manual states the liver can only process one-third an ounce of alcohol per hour, which is considerably less than the alcohol in a standard drink.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, How Alcohol Works

question: According to the manual, which of the following drinks contain roughly the same amount of alcohol?
choice_a: Only beer and liquor, but not wine
choice_b: A 12-ounce beer and a full bottle of wine
choice_c: A 12-ounce glass of 5% beer, a 5-ounce glass of 12% wine, and a 1.5-ounce shot of 80-proof liquor
choice_d: None of these drinks are comparable in alcohol content
explanation: The manual states that a 12-ounce glass of 5% beer, a 5-ounce glass of 12% wine, and a 1.5-ounce shot of 80-proof liquor all contain the same amount of alcohol.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, What Is a Drink?

question: What three factors does the manual say determine Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC)?
choice_a: The time of day, the temperature, and your driving experience
choice_b: Your age, your gender, and the type of vehicle you drive
choice_c: Only the type of alcoholic beverage consumed
choice_d: The amount of alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight
explanation: The manual states BAC is determined by the amount of alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your weight.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, What Determines Blood Alcohol Concentration?

question: Which part of the brain does the manual say alcohol affects first as BAC builds up?
choice_a: The part that controls judgment and self-control
choice_b: The part that controls breathing only
choice_c: Alcohol affects the whole brain equally and simultaneously
choice_d: The part that controls long-term memory only
explanation: The manual states the first part of the brain affected controls judgment and self-control, which can keep drinkers from knowing they are getting drunk.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol and the Brain

question: Which of the following driving effects does the manual link to increasing BAC?
choice_a: Straddling lanes, quick jerky starts, and running stop signs and red lights
choice_b: Increased ability to judge distances accurately
choice_c: No observable change in driving behavior below .10 BAC
choice_d: Perfectly smooth lane changes and improved reaction time
explanation: The manual lists straddling lanes, quick jerky starts, and running stop signs and red lights among the effects of increasing BAC on driving.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Alcohol and the Brain

question: What kinds of drugs does the manual say laws prohibit being under the influence of while on duty?
choice_a: Only prescription medications, but not over-the-counter drugs
choice_b: Only illegal narcotics, but not amphetamines
choice_c: Any controlled substance, amphetamines, narcotics, or any other substance that can make the driver unsafe
choice_d: The manual places no restrictions on any drug use while on duty
explanation: The manual states laws prohibit being under the influence of any controlled substance, amphetamines, narcotics, or any other substance that can make the driver unsafe.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Other Drugs

question: When is possession and use of a drug given to a driver by a doctor permitted, according to the manual?
choice_a: Never, regardless of doctor's instructions
choice_b: Only if the driver is off duty for the entire trip
choice_c: Only for over-the-counter cold medicines, not prescriptions
choice_d: When the doctor informs the driver that it will not affect safe driving ability
explanation: The manual states possession and use of a doctor-prescribed drug is permitted if the doctor informs the driver it will not affect safe driving ability.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Other Drugs

question: What does the manual say about common over-the-counter cold medicines?
choice_a: They are banned entirely for commercial drivers
choice_b: They have no effect on driving ability whatsoever
choice_c: They may make the driver drowsy or otherwise affect safe driving ability
choice_d: They are always safe regardless of dosage
explanation: The manual notes that prescription and over-the-counter drugs such as cold medicines may make the driver drowsy or otherwise affect safe driving ability.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Other Drugs

question: What does the manual say is the only cure for fatigue?
choice_a: Cold water on the face
choice_b: Rest
choice_c: Caffeine
choice_d: A drug that hides fatigue symptoms
explanation: The manual states you should not use any drug that hides fatigue, because the only cure for fatigue is rest.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Other Drugs

question: According to the manual, what should you do if you become too ill to operate a motor vehicle safely?
choice_a: You must not drive, though in an emergency you may drive to the nearest place you can safely stop
choice_b: You must always continue to your final destination regardless of illness
choice_c: Illness has no bearing on whether you should drive
choice_d: You should only stop driving if a passenger insists
explanation: The manual states that if you become too ill to drive safely, you must not drive, but in an emergency you may drive to the nearest place you can safely stop.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Illness

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers
question: What must all commercial drivers, not just those with a hazmat endorsement, be able to do regarding hazardous cargo?
choice_a: Recognize hazardous cargo and know whether they can haul it without a hazardous materials endorsement
choice_b: Personally test cargo chemicals before loading
choice_c: Memorize the entire Emergency Response Guidebook
choice_d: Only hazmat-endorsed drivers need to know anything about hazardous materials
explanation: The manual states all drivers should know something about hazardous materials, be able to recognize hazardous cargo, and know whether they can haul it without a hazmat endorsement.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Hazardous Materials Rules For All Commercial Drivers

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers
question: How does the manual define hazardous materials?
choice_a: Only materials that are explosive
choice_b: Products that pose a risk to health, safety, and property during transportation
choice_c: Only materials regulated by local city ordinances
choice_d: Any cargo weighing more than 10,000 pounds
explanation: The manual defines hazardous materials as products that pose a risk to health, safety, and property during transportation.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, What Are Hazardous Materials?

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers
question: What three intents does the manual say hazardous materials rules serve?
choice_a: Only to communicate the risk; containment and safe equipment are not addressed
choice_b: Increase shipping speed, reduce paperwork, and lower insurance costs
choice_c: Contain the product, communicate the risk, and ensure safe drivers and equipment
choice_d: Standardize truck colors, limit driving hours, and reduce fuel costs
explanation: The manual states the intent of hazardous materials rules is to contain the product, communicate the risk, and ensure safe drivers and equipment.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Why Are There Rules?

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers
question: Where does the manual say hazardous materials shipping papers may be kept while driving?
choice_a: In the trailer with the cargo
choice_b: Locked in the glove compartment out of sight
choice_c: In the sleeper berth only
choice_d: In a pouch on the driver's door, or in clear view within reach
explanation: The manual states shipping papers must be kept in a pouch on the driver's door, in clear view within reach while driving, or on the driver's seat when out of the vehicle.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Why Are There Rules?

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers
question: What is a placard, as described in the manual?
choice_a: A logbook entry describing cargo weight
choice_b: A permit carried only by the shipper, not the vehicle
choice_c: A sign put on the outside of a vehicle that identifies the hazard class of the cargo
choice_d: A sticker placed only on the shipping papers
explanation: The manual defines placards as signs put on the outside of a vehicle that identify the hazard class of the cargo.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Lists of Regulated Products

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers
question: How many identical placards must a placarded vehicle have, and where are they placed?
choice_a: As many as the driver chooses, with no fixed placement
choice_b: Exactly two, placed only on the rear
choice_c: Exactly one, placed on the front bumper
choice_d: At least four, placed on the front, rear, and both sides
explanation: The manual states a placarded vehicle must have at least four identical placards, placed on the front, rear, and both sides.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Lists of Regulated Products

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers
question: What are identification numbers, as described in the manual?
choice_a: A two-letter state code identifying the shipper
choice_b: A four-digit code used by first responders to identify hazardous materials, preceded by 'NA' or 'UN'
choice_c: The driver's CDL license number
choice_d: A number found only on the bill of lading, never on the vehicle
explanation: The manual describes identification numbers as a four-digit code preceded by 'NA' or 'UN' used by first responders to identify hazardous materials.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Lists of Regulated Products

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers
question: Can a driver without a hazardous materials endorsement drive a vehicle carrying hazardous materials, according to the manual?
choice_a: Only if the driver has at least five years of experience
choice_b: Yes, as long as the load does not require placards
choice_c: No, any driver hauling any amount of hazardous material must have the endorsement
choice_d: Only on interstate highways, never on state roads
explanation: The manual states you can drive a vehicle carrying hazardous materials if it does not require placards, but if it requires placards, you cannot drive it without the hazardous materials endorsement.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Lists of Regulated Products

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers
question: What must a driver pass to obtain the hazardous materials endorsement, according to the manual?
choice_a: A physical strength test
choice_b: Only a road skills test, with no written component
choice_c: No test is required, only an application fee
choice_d: A written test on material found in Section 9 of the manual
explanation: The manual states that to get the hazardous materials endorsement, a driver must pass a written test on material found in Section 9 of the manual.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Lists of Regulated Products

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers
question: What capacity threshold does the manual give for requiring a tank endorsement?
choice_a: Only tanks carrying hazardous liquids, regardless of size
choice_b: Any tank of any size attached to a commercial vehicle
choice_c: An individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate capacity of 1,000 gallons or more
choice_d: An individual rated capacity of more than 500 gallons only
explanation: The manual specifies a tank endorsement is required for a vehicle designed to transport liquid or gaseous materials in a tank or tanks with an individual rated capacity of more than 119 gallons and an aggregate capacity of 1,000 gallons or more.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Lists of Regulated Products

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers
question: What does the manual say happens if you drive a vehicle needing placards without a hazardous materials endorsement and are stopped?
choice_a: There are no real consequences as long as no accident occurs
choice_b: Only the shipper, never the driver, faces consequences
choice_c: You only receive a written warning the first time
choice_d: You will be cited and not allowed to drive your truck, costing time and money
explanation: The manual warns that driving a vehicle needing placards without the endorsement is a crime, and if stopped you will be cited and not allowed to drive your truck, costing time and money.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Lists of Regulated Products

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers
question: Before loading a truck with more than one type of hazardous product, what does the manual say you must know?
choice_a: Only the total weight of the combined load
choice_b: Whether it is safe to load them together, and if unsure, ask your employer and consult the regulations
choice_c: Nothing; all hazardous products can always be loaded together
choice_d: Only the destination address
explanation: The manual instructs that before loading more than one type of product, you must know if it is safe to load them together, and if unsure, ask your employer and consult the regulations.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Lists of Regulated Products

topic: Hazardous Materials Rules for All Commercial Drivers
question: According to the manual's hazard class chart, corrosives such as hydrochloric acid and battery fluid fall under which class?
choice_a: Class 1
choice_b: Class 4
choice_c: Class 8
choice_d: Class 7
explanation: The manual's hazard class chart lists Class 8 as Corrosives, with examples including hydrochloric acid and battery fluid.
source_note: Montana Commercial Driver License Manual, Section 2 - Driving Safely, Lists of Regulated Products
